relevance_note: Letter describing one patient with compound heterozygous LPIN2 variants and his carrier parents: "we reported a Chinese patient with Majeed syndrome due to a novel compound heterozygous variant in LPIN2".
method_note: Read the whole letter by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading. No PMID: 'N88' from the 'Record: N88' header. The single patient is called 'The proband' (role word), so labelled 'patient' (rule 5); the parents are 'father of patient' and 'mother of patient' (rule 2) and are in scope as tested relatives (Sanger sequencing). Markdown escapes: the paper prints '>' as '>' in most places and once as fullwidth '＞' (WES sentence); the transcript is printed 'NM\_014646.2' (Markdown escape). Values are written with '>' and 'NM_014646.2'; spans keep the paper's characters. Possible inconsistency: after stating father carries c.2534delG and mother carries c.1966A>G, the paper says 'the two mutations in the proband were from his mother and father, respectively', which in listing order (c.2534delG, c.1966A>G) would reverse the parents; inheritance follows the explicit carrier statement. Variant type for c.2534delG left 'not reported': the authors call it 'a deletion mutation' (no matching enum class; frameshift not stated). Pathogenicity and functional statements not copied to the parents' rows (said for the proband's variants, D-29). Not recorded: fever ('the temperature decreased to normal' implies raised temperature but no fever is stated); WBC 10.5 x 10^9/L (no interpretation given). Knee effusion recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'joint or limb swelling' left not reported (imaging finding). 'Osteoarticular pain' marked as both bone pain and joint pain on the checklist. CRP 44.6 mg/L marked as elevated inflammatory marker although the paper gives no normal range for CRP. Age at onset not stated (first admission at 18 months recorded as onset of the walking problem only). Parents' phenotypes are not described; the pedigree figure is not available as text.
